cards.text: Most apps follow rules that people wrote
AI learns its own patterns from examples
You already use it every day

steps.question: A music app picks your next song
steps.why: It learns from what you play and skip.
steps.learnMore: Apps like this compare your listening with lots of other people's to guess what you'll like.

steps.question: Which ones use AI?
steps.why: AI learned from examples. The others follow fixed steps.
steps.learnMore: A calculator gives the same answer every time because someone wrote the exact rules for it.

steps.why: Lots of apps just follow fixed rules.
steps.learnMore: An alarm clock app feels smart, but it only does what its rules say: ring at the time you set.

cards.text: Then it guesses on new ones

steps.question: How does AI learn?
steps.why: AI finds patterns in lots of examples.
steps.learnMore: Show it thousands of cat photos and it works out which shapes usually mean a cat.

steps.question: Which teaches AI more?
steps.learnMore: Variety matters too. Photos of one cat won't teach it about every cat.

steps.question: What helps AI learn cats?
steps.why: Clear examples teach. Empty ones don't.
steps.learnMore: A label tells AI what a photo shows, so it knows which pattern to look for.

steps.statement: AI trained only on cats would know dogs
steps.why: It only knows patterns it has seen.
steps.learnMore: Show it a dog and it may just guess cat, because that's all it has.

cards.text: A chatbot guesses what comes next
Then it repeats, piece by piece

steps.question: Peanut butter and...
steps.why: You guessed the likely next word, like a chatbot does.
steps.learnMore: Chatbots really work with small pieces of words, called tokens.

steps.question: You ask a chatbot the same thing twice
steps.why: It can pick a different likely word each time.
steps.learnMore: Most chatbots add a little randomness so their writing doesn't sound like a copy.

steps.statement: A chatbot looks up every answer in a book of facts
steps.why: It predicts words. It isn't reading from a fact list.
steps.learnMore: Some chatbots can also search the web, but they still write by predicting.

cards.text: AI can make up facts and sources
So check anything that has to be true

steps.statement: If AI sounds sure, it's right
steps.why: It sounds just as sure when it's wrong.
steps.learnMore: It's built to write likely words, and a confident tone is very common in what it learned from.

steps.question: Use it, or check it first?
steps.why: Check anything that has to be true.
steps.learnMore: For health questions, talk to a doctor, school nurse or another adult you trust.

steps.question: AI gives you a source. Now what?
steps.why: AI can invent sources that look real.
steps.learnMore: Search for the exact title. If you can't find it anywhere, don't use it.
